newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy's Prodi visits rebel-held Albanian town.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi visits rebel-held Albanian town.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi paid a lightning visit to a rebel-held Albanian town on Wednesday for talks with his Albanian counterpart Bashkim Fino on preparing an Italian-led force to protect aid supplies.

Witnesses said Prodi arrived by helicopter in Gjirokaster, a southern town where Fino was formerly mayor of the opposition Socialist party. The town now is run by a rebel committee after an insurrection in Albania last month.
An official at the Gjirokaster town hall, contacted by telephone, said that Prodi met Fino for about half and hour and then left again by helicopter. Fino is due to leave later for talks in Greece.
Rome is preparing a force of some 5,000 troops to protect supplies of food and medicine to Albania, facing its worst crisis since the collapse of communism in 1990.

Italy and Albania are also seeking to smooth relations after an Albanian refugee boat sank in the Adriatic last week after a collision with an Italian navy corvette. Tirana says that at least 80 people died.

Fino was warmly greeted by rebels bristling with guns when he arrived in the town on Tuesday. Right-wing President Sali Berisha has accused parties in a new unity government, including the Socialists, of siding with rebels against him.
